page: Microsoft Azure E2as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V, designed for workloads requiring a high memory-to-vCPU ratio. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, running on an AMD EPYC 7763 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. Cache allocation comprises 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 16.0 GB, delivering 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance includes 34 GB of local SSD temporary storage and features no hardware graphics accelerators (0 GPUs). Supported CPU extensions include standard AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, while lacking AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread capability counterbalanced by constraints in aggregate compute and parallel throughput. In stress-ng, single-core CPU performance tests achieved 2703.88, categorizing it in the top 25%. However, multi-core metrics reflect the low vCPU ceiling, placing multi-core stress-ng (2703.88) and Geekbench multi-core (1959.0) in the bottom percentiles. Single-threaded operations like gzip compression (26.04 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (11.08 GB/sec) fell within average brackets, whereas highly parallel tasks such as Clang compilation (1976.0), ray tracing (2298.0), and PassMark physics (397.23) scored in the bottom 10%. Memory subsystem bandwidth is relatively constrained, recording 32.67 GB/sec for large block uncached reads and 22.32 GB/sec for uncached writes.

Regarding qualitative cost efficiency, the E2as_v4 offers an accessible entry point to the memory-dense EASv4 line, granting 16 GB of memory across a minimal compute footprint. While it delivers viable efficiency for memory-resident workloads that do not demand extensive core counts, it exhibits notable tradeoffs. Throughput-dependent applications register lower metrics, including static web serving throughput (2.48 GB/sec), Redis SET operations (2.03 million ops/sec), and small-model prompt inference (136.84 tokens/sec).

Consequently, the Azure E2as_v4 fits small memory-intensive services, light in-memory caching nodes, staging databases, background queue workers, and moderate general-purpose tasks that necessitate 16 GB of RAM without requiring multi-core parallel scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure E2as_v4 is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs and 1 physical core from an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz, equipped with 32 MB of L3 cache. With 16.0 GB of system memory, it achieves an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, paired with 34 GB of local SSD temporary storage and zero GPUs. Benchmark data illustrates capable single-core execution, ranking in the top 25% on single-core stress-ng, alongside average single-threaded compression speeds. Conversely, the 2-vCPU configuration limits parallel performance, resulting in lower tiers for multi-core Geekbench, PassMark physics, software compilation, and uncached memory bandwidth. Cost efficiency is balanced toward low-footprint services requiring substantial memory overhead without heavy compute utilization. The instance is suitable for small in-memory caches, lightweight relational databases, and low-scale memory-intensive background tasks.
